title: Handover and rebooking
audience: Residential cleaners who hand over a clean to the household and arrange the next visit.
learningOutcomes: Walk the client through the completed work and the exclusions.
Record the handover, including any issues found and not fixed.
Offer rebooking on the agreed terms, without promising work that is not scoped.

instruction.heading: Walking the client through
instruction.body: At handover, walk the client through the completed rooms and the exclusions. Say what was done and what was not, and point out any issue that you found and could not fix, such as a damaged fitting or a stain that did not respond to the approved method. Let the client see the areas that you are reporting.

instruction.heading: Recording the handover
instruction.body: Record the handover with the time, the rooms covered, the exclusions, the issues found and the client's acknowledgement. Keep the record factual. Do not describe the home as sterile or as free of pests, and do not guarantee a result beyond the scope.

instruction.heading: Rebooking
instruction.body: Offer a rebooking on the agreed terms, and confirm the scope for the next visit against the current record. Do not promise extra tasks that have not been scoped and priced. If the client wants a different scope, note the change for approval.

procedure: Walk the client through the completed rooms and the exclusions.
Point out any issue found and not fixed, and show the affected area.
Record the time, rooms, exclusions, issues and client acknowledgement.
Keep the record factual, with no sterility or pest-free claim.
Offer rebooking on agreed terms, and note any scope change for approval.

workedExamples.situation: A stain in the bathroom did not respond to the approved method, and the client asks you to promise it will be gone next time.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you say and record?
workedExamples.reasoning: Explain that the stain did not respond to the approved method, and record it as an issue not fixed. Do not promise removal next time. Offer to assess the stain at the next visit, and note any specialist option for the client to consider.

equipmentAndPpe: Camera for issue photographs, with permission.

commonErrors.error: Describing the home as sterile after cleaning.
commonErrors.prevention: Describe only the clean and the exclusions.

commonErrors.error: Promising removal of a stain at the next visit.
commonErrors.prevention: Record the issue and offer an assessment.

commonErrors.error: Agreeing extra tasks at the door without pricing.
commonErrors.prevention: Note the request and price it for approval.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Content is general cleaning practice and needs subject-matter and regulator review before use.

Under the Australian Consumer Law, a business must not mislead consumers about a service. Claims need to be correct and have a sound basis, intent does not matter, and a statement that gives a misleading picture can break the law (ACCC false or misleading claims page; page metadata dates it 28 June 2026). A cleaner cannot verify pest-free or sterile outcomes, so do not make those statements. Consumer guarantees also require a service to be carried out competently, at the standard an average competent provider would reach, and in a sensible timeframe where no time is agreed (ACCC consumer rights and guarantees page for businesses; page metadata dates it 17 July 2026).

qualityStandard: Handover walk-through completed with exclusions shown.
Issues not fixed recorded factually in the case study.
Rebooking offered on the agreed scope only.
documentationEvidence: Signed handover record with time, rooms, exclusions and issues.
Rebooking note with the agreed scope.
summary: Walk the client through the work and the exclusions.
Record issues not fixed and keep the record factual.
Rebook on the agreed scope only.

knowledgeChecks.question: A stain did not respond to the approved method. What is correct at handover?
options: Record it as an issue not fixed, and offer an assessment
Promise it will be gone next time, for sure, by the next visit
Hide it under a towel until the client has left the house

knowledgeChecks.question: Which statement should a cleaner avoid at handover?
options: That the rooms in scope were cleaned
That the home is sterile or pest-free

knowledgeChecks.question: A client asks for an extra room at rebooking. What is correct?
options: Agree at the door, since it is only a small job
Refuse without comment, since the room is not booked
Note it, and price and approve it before it is booked
